sentences.text: Shri Harshad Bahirani, learned counsel for the applicant.
Shri Manoj Dwivedi, learned Public Prosecutor for the respondent/State.
Case Diary is perused.
Learned counsel for the rival parties are heard.
The applicant has filed this second application under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of anticipatory bail.
The first application was dismissed on merits vide order dated 13/11/2019 passed in MCRC No.45492/2019.

The applicant apprehends his arrest in connection with Crime No.382/2019 registered at Police Station- Ambah, District- Morena for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 272, 273 and 120- B of IPC and Sections 51 and 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

Allegations against the applicant, in short, are that he along with co-accused Banwarilal Sharma was found involved in manufacturing food unsafe for human consumption at Milk Chiller Center of the co-accused, wherefrom two tankers containing 12000 litres of milk and a loading vehicle carrying 15 sacks of Exetrin powder were seized.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant has been falsely implicated.
He is neither the owner of the Tankers nor of the business.
The offences are triable by JMFC.
Except section 420 of the IPC and 51 and 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, the rest are bailable in nature.
There is no allegation of cheating against the applicant.
Nothing has been seized from the applicant.
There is no likelihood of his absconsion or tampering with the evidence.

With the aforesaid submissions,

1 prayer for anticipatory bail is made.

sentences.text: Learned Public Prosecutor for the State opposed the application and prayed for its rejection by contending that on the basis of the allegations and the material available on record, no case for grant of anticipatory bail is made out.

It is also submitted by the learned counsel for the respondent/State that the investigation is pending and custodial interrogation may be required in the matter and the submission made by the counsel for the applicant has already been considered in previous bail application which was rejected by this Court.
The perusal of the earlier bail rejection order reveals that this Court has already gone through the record and has passed the order on the merits of the case.
It was not found to be a fit case where the accused could be released on bail.
The law on the point of repeat bail is well settled.
Unless there is a fresh ground, a new bail application cannot be successfully moved.
It is also well settled that a fresh ground does not mean a new argument by the same counsel or a new argument by another counsel who may be subsequently engaged.
Fresh ground means a ground which did not exist at, at the time of hearing of the earlier bail application.

Therefore, after considering the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties and circumstances of the case, without expressing any view on the merits of the matter, it would be apparent that no new ground or change in circumstances could be shown by the applicant so that the view taken on 13/11/2019 may be changed.
On the basis of aforesaid, it is not a good case in which the applicant may be released on anticipatory bail.
Consequently, this second anticipatory bail application under Section 438 of Cr.P.C filed by the applicant is hereby dismissed.

(S.A. Dharmadhikari) Judge rahul RAHUL SINGH PARIHAR 2020.01.09 11:40:18 +05'30'
